routeSplit.status: NEW ROUTE — the single judgment call in this PR, flagged for review
routeSplit.justification: Pure resolution read: symbol in, node id out. It is resolve_security(mint=False) — the same alias era-walk, the same bitemporal as-of gate, the same ambiguity tie-break as /securities/resolve, with the step-5 provisional mint replaced by an honest absence. It exists because TW-25's stated capability (ticker or CME root to a node id, for a service caller) collides with the rule that anything minting stays operator: /securities/resolve is read-then-mint-on-miss, so serving it would hand a service caller the power to create identity through a GET, and would break TW-24's test that pins /securities/resolve as unreachable by a service caller. Splitting the read half out satisfies both.

The dispatch's named example: a merge-following lookup, node id in, terminal-survivor node id out. It does contain a write (spec-2.8 path compression rewrites intermediate merge links and flushes) but nothing on this request path commits, and get_db closes the session without committing — pinned by test_no_served_route_commits_anything rather than asserted.
Pure read: node id in, its currently-open alias-era symbol out. Calls canonical() first, so it carries the same non-committing property.

MINTS. Spec 2.2 step 5 creates a provisional node when nothing matches, writes a symbol-alias atom, and commits. Also the route TW-24's test pins as unreachable by a service caller, so widening it would have changed TW-24's behaviour.

MINTS, and writes on a HIT as well as a miss: an existing option node still gets _ensure_edge('derives_from') plus a commit, and the underlying is resolved through resolve_security which may itself mint.
MINTS an issuer node on every miss (resolved when keyed on LEI, provisional on the name-fuzzy fallback) and CLAIMS the LEI in the global identifier index. Identifier claiming is identity creation.

routeSplitNotes: Six routes total: the five that existed on the securities router plus /securities/lookup.
The blanket 'app.include_router(securities_router, dependencies=[Depends(require_operator)])' in main.py is REMOVED, not narrowed. Nothing is protected by inheritance any more.
Sorted by the rule as given: mixed read-then-mint routes were sorted as MUTATING, per 'when in doubt, it stays operator'.
Nothing widened to anonymous. Every route is behind operator or user-or-service.
GET /spine/anchor/verify/{atom_id} untouched. Its two TW-24 guards (status + dependency-graph) still pass.

Adjacent operator surface deliberately NOT touched: the 10 /admin/nodes + /admin/resolver/* routes in app/routers/admin_securities.py read the same Node/Edge/IdentifierIndex/MergeLink substrate and keep their own router-level require_operator. A test asserts a service caller gets 403 on all 10.

filesChanged.detail: Removed the router-level dependencies=[Depends(require_operator)] on securities_router; replaced with a comment naming the per-route split. Dropped the now-unused 'Depends' and 'require_operator' imports (no other main.py registration used them).
Per-route dependencies via two named module constants (SERVED / OPERATOR); new GET /securities/lookup; module docstring rewritten to state the split and why each resolve* route is a write.

resolve_security gains a KEYWORD-ONLY 'mint: bool = True'. Default is the historical behaviour byte for byte; mint=False returns an honest absence at step 5 instead of minting. All 20 existing call sites pass venue/asof/asset_class by keyword and are unaffected.
30 tests: the five required negatives, the write-proofs, three structural guards, and the cross-repo ULID contract pin.

ulidFormatCheck.flaggedNotAChange: The cockpit can also mint evt_, wallet_, token_ and contract_ ids via get_or_create_typed_node. All four are REJECTED by the contract's NodeIdSchema, which is correct today because none is an instrument. But note the name trap: the cockpit's 'contract_' prefix means an ON-CHAIN CONTRACT ADDRESS (crypto), while smart-markets' 'contract' SHAPE is a futures contract addressed by a sec_ id (TwinNodeSchema.id = SecurityNodeIdSchema for all three shapes). A futures node in the cockpit is minted through resolve_security as kind 'security', so it is sec_-prefixed and correct — but do not wire the cockpit's contract_ kind to the twin's contract shape. Reported, not acted on.

blocked.severity: blocks one third of TW-25's own acceptance criterion
blocked.detail: _rd_disclosure_twin/08_build_scope.md row TW-25 requires 'Ticker, CIK, and CME root each resolve to a node identifier through a non-operator path.' Ticker and CME root are delivered (both are symbols; GET /securities/lookup resolves them, and a futures node is sec_-prefixed via the same path). CIK IS NOT, and cannot be delivered by any gating change, because CIK -> node resolution does not exist in the security master for ANY principal, operator included.
evidence: app/models.py:1102 — IdentifierIndex docstring: 'identifier_type in {figi,cusip,isin,lei}'; column comment on line 1112 the same.
The Node model has no cik column (columns: node_id, node_type, asset_class, current_symbol, primary_venue, identifiers_json, lei, name, status, resolution_status, contract_json, created_at).
_index_identifier is called with 'figi', 'cusip', 'isin', 'lei' only (resolver.py 381, 1273, 1391, 1502; jobs/resolver_backfill.py 217). Never with 'cik'.
'cik' appears in app/ only inside app/providers/edgar.py (a ticker->CIK map used to fetch EDGAR submissions) and on filing rows in the backfill jobs. It is never indexed against a node.
blocked.recommendation: Its own build row, not a re-gate. edgar.symbol_to_cik() already provides ticker->CIK, so the cheap shape is: index 'cik' into IdentifierIndex during the base-library backfill, widen the documented identifier_type set, then expose an id_type/value form on the served /securities/lookup. Left entirely alone here — inventing a CIK index inside a gating PR would have been the wrong call.
blocked.note: This is a contract/scope question for the planner, in the same spirit as the ULID instruction: report it loudly, do not bend the resolver to fit.

judgmentCallForReview.what: Added GET /securities/lookup rather than only re-gating the five existing routes.
judgmentCallForReview.why: The dispatch's two rules collide on this router. 'Resolution READS (identifier in, node id out) become get_user_or_service_caller' describes /securities/resolve exactly. 'Anything that MUTATES or mints stays require_operator, when in doubt it stays operator' also describes /securities/resolve exactly, because it is read-then-mint-on-miss. Serving it as-is would have (a) let a service caller create identity through a GET, breaking the hard constraint that a service caller must never reach a mutating route, and (b) broken TW-24's test that pins /securities/resolve as unreachable by a service caller, which the dispatch forbids. Sorting it to operator and stopping there would have satisfied both rules and delivered nothing: no service caller could resolve a ticker, which is the entire point of the row and the reason _decisions/2026-08-16_instrument_scope_identifier.md names TW-25 as a prerequisite.
judgmentCallForReview.shape: The addition is minimal and reversible: one route, one keyword-only resolver parameter defaulting to today's behaviour, zero changes to any existing route's semantics. Deleting the route and the mint parameter restores a pure re-gate.
judgmentCallForReview.strike: If the planner disagrees, strike /securities/lookup and the mint parameter; the remaining split (canonical + current-symbol served, three resolve* routes operator) stands on its own and needs no rework.
